entries.title: 17. Post-production & delivery
entries.outputIntent: Source knowledge for review + assembly + finishing + audio and rights metadata
guidance:
## 17. Post-production & delivery
🟢 **Upscale ladder:** (1) bring the source still to max quality BEFORE video generation (a 4K anchor still gives the model detail budget). (2) Video upscaling as its own pass: Topaz Video AI is reference class; model by material: **Astra for AI-generated video**, Proteus generic, Iris faces, Starlight heavy degradation, Apollo/Aion interpolation/slow-motion. Alternatives integrated in Resolve/Premiere; open-source Video2X/Real-ESRGAN. Judge one exported frame before batch renders. [W]
🟡 **Frame-rate caveat on upscale [P34]:** practitioners run Topaz at 4K/60 fps for cartoons — interpolation erases the deliberate 12-fps judder of stop-motion and limited-animation looks; keep the native frame rate for claymation/anime/limited styles, interpolate only for smooth 3D looks.
🟢 **Grading as the final pass** over the edited film (not per clip) — unifying palette/contrast is the strongest single lever against the "assembled" feel.
🟢 **Exposure matching across generations:** shared master plates + identical Kelvin/exposure lines in every prompt of a location (the multi-plate set at ONE shared exposure, platforms-models ch. 13b; the white-balance Kelvin value fixed per scene, video-prompting ch. 12c) keep takes gradable; residual mismatch is normal and belongs to the grading pass — never re-generate for exposure alone.
🟢 **Trim rule:** AI clips have soft starts/ends — trim the first and last ~0.5 s per clip. [H-off] Post step on the assembled cut only: chaining and extension take their boundary frame from the raw export (video-prompting ch. 14). At a chain join both sides hold the same pose, so trim the outgoing soft tail and the incoming soft head as ONE cut point and confirm the action still reads continuous — restore frames if it jumps.
🟡 **Music bleed in post [P38]:** a dominant real score masks bled model music, but lowering the clip's volume kills its SFX too — re-add SFX manually.
🟢 **Frame-rate drops in generated takes (Seedance 2.0, feature-scale evidence) [H-off, P47, P49]:** despite "24 fps" in the prompt, takes came back stuttering at ~12–18 fps; fix in the NLE by deleting the duplicated frames — the audio track is cut with them, so such takes serve as B-roll only (≈4 s lost per take). Check 2.5 takes frame by frame before assuming the issue is gone.
🟡 **Anti-plastic finishing pass [P20]:** (1) cut the model's unmotivated slow-motion — it reads as fake; (2) edit-side punch-ins/outs (100 → ~120 % over the clip) as cheap camera moves — only on 2K+/upscaled sources, a 1080p master loses visible resolution; (3) a light noise/grain overlay per clip — the strongest per-clip lever against plastic (the grade stays the film-level lever); (4) subtle edge blur/vignette. Small doses; grain first. Aspect changes (letterboxing) are a master-ratio decision (format strategy below), not a finishing trick.
🟢 **Master strategy:** master at highest available quality (ProRes/H.265 high bitrate); derive deliveries. Archive original generations + final prompts (re-render capability).
🟡 **Format strategy:** fix the master aspect ratio BEFORE production; plan multi-format derivation (3:4/4:3-near sources allow the widest crops); compose critical content inside the tightest target crop's safe area. For video generations the ratio is a platform setting, never prompt text; image prompts state canvas + ratio first (style-control §2).

entries.title: 18. Audio post: music, SFX, voices
entries.outputIntent: Source knowledge for review + assembly + finishing + audio and rights metadata
guidance:
## 18. Audio post: music, SFX, voices
🟢 **Three legitimate music paths** (choice = rights question, not just sound):
1. **Self-produced** — DAW/composition route incl. AI-assisted vocal/instrument synthesis (e.g. ACE Studio): full rights, full control, score composed to picture. Cleanest path for ambitious projects.
2. **Classically licensed** — library/stock music or commissioned score with sync license.
3. **Generative** (Suno, Udio, ElevenLabs Music, Stable Audio 3, AIVA) — with licensing caution: paid plans grant a **usage license to the output, not copyright ownership**; free tiers exclude commercial use; the legal landscape is in motion (label suits/settlements). Licensing-first options: ElevenLabs Music and Stable Audio 3 (licensed training data; Stable Audio adds an SFX model and open weights), AIVA for orchestral/MIDI export. ⚠️ Udio is currently a walled garden (downloads disabled). Read the terms BEFORE any commercial release. [W]
🟢 **MiniMax Music 3 (open-weights release Aug 2026):** creative concept + optional lyrics → a complete, structurally coherent song up to 5 min in one generation, 32 kHz/16-bit stereo; hybrid architecture (8B global LLM initialized from Qwen3-8B modeling long-range song structure + a second LM + continuous synthesis stage); design focus: sustained expressive intent across the full track, physically realistic instruments, vocals that read as performed rather than synthesized. Hosted API: `music-3.0` at $0.15/generation (up to 5 min), `music-3.0-free` at 3 req/min, lyrics generation $0.01 — the lowest published per-track price of current frontier music vendors. Family tools: Music 2.5 adds paragraph-level structure control (14+ tags: Intro/Bridge/Hook/Build-up…) and instrumental-only mode; a dedicated cover/remix model reworks 6-s–6-min reference audio with automatic ASR lyric extraction — rights in the source material are YOURS to clear. **Open weights = pipeline ownership** (runs in ComfyUI — the music equivalent of Wan on the video side). ⚠️ Licensing story is thin (training-data provenance undocumented) — apply the same commercial caution as the rest of this bucket. 🟡 Availability on aggregators (Higgsfield, fal & co.) is expected but unverified at time of writing — check current hosting before planning. [W: official MiniMax research blog + ComfyUI + API docs]
🟢 **Score rule:** never generate music inside the video model (production-pipeline ch. 6) — the score is built over the edited film; the music on the timeline then dictates re-cut needs. Diegetic sound comes from generation; fill gaps via SFX libraries or SFX generators.
🟢 **In-model voice harvesting (Seedance, production-proven) [P17]:** the FIRST generation sets the voice baseline per character — keeping it consistent afterwards is the actual challenge. Workflow: (1) trim every spoken line of a character out of the generated takes; (2) compile them into ONE per-character voice reference, combined length UNDER 30 s; (3) where the surface has an audio-reference slot, export the compilation as an audio file and attach it as `@Audio`; where the surface takes only video references, export as **MP4 with a black screen — not MP3** — and attach it as `@Video`. Either way it gets the role line from the voice-channel rule (video-prompting ch. 14b) — the black clip must be declared "voice only, not a motion reference"; attach it alongside the character sheet in every following generation where the character speaks. Voices then hold across generations and extends.
🟢 **Voice consistency as a system:** per character one **voice profile** (description in the prompt sheet + where available a cloned/saved voice, e.g. a voice library — this is the reference half of the voice channel; the written description is the text half, both travel together, video-prompting ch. 14b voice channel) instead of re-rolling voices per shot. Accept the native generation voice where it fits (the sheet locks it); for control: re-record the dialogue track via TTS/voice clone and replace in the edit — lip-sync realignment via dedicated tools when on-camera. Expressivity: stability low for character delivery (~0.25), mid for narration (~0.4); always the newest speech model (older ones sound flatter). 🟢 **Voice-changer path for character voicing:** perform the line YOURSELF (timing, emphasis, emotion = directing work) and convert via speech-to-speech into the character voice — preserves intonation and cadence, beats pure TTS for acted scenes; multiple characters from one performer are possible. [W]
🟢 **Performed music: the track is the performance, not a guide [H-off, P24]:** a video model will not perform a song — "rap" yields a mouth moving to nothing. Record the track first, cut it into ~12-second blocks on the vocalist's breaths (⚠️ exceeds the 5–10 s clip range of 12b/14b — one block per take, check the live upload hint), attach each block as an audio file and declare it in plain words: "THE TRACK THEY ARE PERFORMING — the audio of this file IS the live performance." The explanatory version ("audio guide, for sync only") was true and produced nothing. Assign **mouth ownership** explicitly or everyone in frame mouths the verse. (The score rule stands: this is diegetic performance, not underscore.)
🟡 **The opposite pole — sung lines generated in-model [P32, sponsored] ⚠️ documented exception to the score rule / SKILL rule 9 (animation only, disposable tune):** per-stage lines marked as delivery (`<sung, fast and bouncy> (line)` — 12b bracket grammar: delivery in < >, the line in ( ); the source's own notation used `{…}`, which 12b reserves for SFX) with a SOUND block "sung in a bright melodic voice rather than spoken; instrumental passages only under non-singing beats". Use only when the tune is not canon and will not be replaced; when the track IS canon, the P24 recorded-track route is the only one that syncs.
🟢 **Non-English dialogue / dubbing:** trigger: only when native in-model dialogue (the default route, SKILL Workflow 1) fails its test take, or the director requires a specific external voice. Two classes — audio dub (voice + timing preserved, NO lip sync: fine for animation/off-camera) vs. video dub with lip-sync realignment (needed on-camera). Voice cloning only with documented consent.
🟢 **Audio finishing:** loudness-normalize the final mix to the target platform — streaming/online typically **−14 LUFS integrated** (YouTube/Spotify class), EU broadcast **−23 LUFS (EBU R128)**, true peak ≤ −1 dBTP; mix dialogue first, then SFX/ambience, score last; keep stems (dialogue/SFX/music) exported separately for fixes and dubs. [established standards]

entries.title: 19. Continuity supervision & sign-off templates
entries.outputIntent: Source knowledge for review + assembly + finishing + audio and rights metadata
guidance:
## 19. Continuity supervision & sign-off templates
🟢 **Continuity ledger as a mandatory document** (the script-supervisor role): one table across all shots — character state (which state sheet), key props (whose hand, what state), time of day/weather, light direction, screen direction per character, emotional state (what the character just experienced). Check against the previous row before every generation; a state change spawns a sheet order (production-pipeline ch. 3), never a prompt wish.
🟡 **Screen-direction repair in the edit [P28]:** when a take violates the stated screen direction (hero right, threat left), mirror the clip in the NLE before regenerating — free, and continuity holds; caveat: mirroring flips readable text and asymmetric props/wardrobe, so check the ledger row first.
🟢 **Anchor discipline** (continuity anchors for identity/prop/light details — not the style anchor): non-negotiable details as short, verbatim-identical anchor sentences early in EVERY prompt; reinforce drifting details in the next prompt instead of patching in post.
🟢 **Copy-ready checklists:**
- **Take verdict order (binding — every other take rule is subordinate to this):** (1) **Hard rejects first:** a slop tell (production-pipeline ch. 10 — plastic skin, drifting faces between cuts, texture shimmer, hectic cutting at hard motion, floating third-person camera) or a pass-1 identity failure = REJECT as the shot's take regardless of performance; harvest clean 2–4 s as coverage (production-pipeline ch. 10), correction into the NEXT prompt. (2) **Rank the survivors by emotion:** among tell-free, identity-stable takes pick by Murch's ladder (film-craft §4) — the take with the right emotion wins over a cleaner take that feels wrong. (3) **Then repair, never reroll, the winner's local faults:** a pass-2 ledger fault (prop state, screen direction, minor light mismatch, a detail wrong in one region/time window) on the ranked winner is a LOCAL fault → workflows W5 (video_edit, NLE mirror above, cutaway) — this is what "near-approved" in W5 means; only a GLOBAL fault (style, light, physics everywhere) goes back to the prompt. "Correction goes into the NEXT prompt" below applies to step (1) and to global faults, not to the winner's local faults.
- **Still sign-off (before motion test):** identity = sheet? · light motivated + direction noted? · no 3D-game look? · material doctrine met? · reverse need settled? · target-crop safe area clear? · Verify line passes?
- **Take sign-off (batch of 4, watch FULLY):** pass 1 identity (recognizable after every cut?) · pass 2 continuity (ledger row met? props constant?) · pass 3 timing (actions inside budget, no padding break?) · pass 4 camera (one move, axis held, no quick-cut hiding?) · pass 5 audio (diegetic only; no generated underscore — an attached performed track or a declared sung-line exception counts as diegetic; sync; mouth ownership held) · pass 6 style (every check of the recipe's Verify line in bible section B2 passes? — a clean but off-recipe take is rejected, production-pipeline ch. 1). Fix the weakest instruction first; correction goes into the NEXT prompt. When the agent cannot view the result, the director answers the six passes in this order and the answers are recorded as the review (SKILL checklist step 7).
- **Motion ladder (model/style approval):** identical character through: subtle portrait → head turn → walk → fast action → interaction. Only after passing, commit the production style.

entries.title: 20. Legal, licensing & disclosure
entries.outputIntent: Source knowledge for review + assembly + finishing + audio and rights metadata
guidance:
## 20. Legal, licensing & disclosure
🟢 **IP baselines** (consolidated): styles are free; named characters/franchises/songs are not (active enforcement documented across studios, anime rights holders, labels). Standard protection: the ANTI-IP prompt block (platforms-models ch. 13b). Director/DoP names as style references are established; "in the spirit of, fully original execution" is the official formula.
🟢 **Real people:** photos only with consent as references; voice cloning only with documented consent; no recognizable third parties without a release.
🟢 **Real-face moderation is a production risk even WITH rights [W, P19]:** most hosted video models and aggregators reject references that contain a real human face — the filter cannot see your release. Plan for it at casting time:
1. **Test acceptance first** — one cheap generation with the sheet on the target platform BEFORE a scene is built around a licensed likeness.
2. **Registry entry** — the person's sheet, the release, and the platform's terms sit together in the bible's asset registry.
3. **Alternative route budgeted** — 🟡 enterprise tiers of aggregators can switch the restriction off for verified customers (practitioner report, [P19]); 🟡 less restrictive individual tools exist (TopView AI, Oxen AI named Sep 2026 — unverified; check terms and output rights first).
4. **Terms caveat, said once** — ⚠️ bypassing a platform's face filter may breach that platform's terms even when the likeness is licensed; the release settles the rights question, not the terms question. Name it to the director once, then follow their call.
5. 🟡 **Face-grid fallback — this IS the terms risk from step 4 (practitioner test on Seedance 2.5 via a third-party aggregator, Sep 2026) [P19]:** a light scratch/grid pattern laid over the face in the character sheet (as if veiled) gets the reference accepted, and the generated character keeps ≈80–85 % of the likeness — the unmodified sheet consistently produced the more accurate character in every paired test (wide two-shot, location scene, dialogue scene). Usable only when exact likeness is not essential: a distinctive costume or silhouette carries identity, the person appears briefly, wides and mediums. NOT for close-ups, dialogue-heavy scenes, or a character that must match exactly across shots — there the loss is visible. A temporary workaround for a legitimate, released production, never the first choice; record it in the decision log.
Note: 🟢 a moderation error can be a false positive from the PROSE, not the images — the vendor's own team cleared an NSFW block by having the LLM rewrite the prompt; failed runs were not charged (Seedance 2.0, [H-off, P49]). 🟡 Moderation reportedly runs in layers on Seedance 2.5 — prompt check plus output check — and blocks violence/blood/horror, brand names and real persons [P39, unverified]; the riskiest beat is generated FIRST (production-pipeline ch. 10).
🟢 **Commercial output rights per platform:** rights hang on the plan (free tiers often non-commercial) and change — read the current terms of the generation platform AND music/voice services before release; budget for moderation/eligibility checks.
🟢 **Copyrightability of AI output:** under current US Copyright Office guidance, purely AI-generated output is **not copyrightable**; protection requires human authorship — creative selection, arrangement, editing, or substantial human-authored elements can be protected as such. EU member states similarly require human creative input. Practical rule: **document your human creative contribution** (treatment, shot design, prompt authorship, edit decisions) — it is your protectable layer and your evidence. [established guidance]
🟢 **Disclosure duty (EU AI Act Art. 50, effective 2026-08-02):** synthetic content that could pass as real needs (a) human-readable disclosure and (b) machine-readable marking; the EU practice code names **C2PA Content Credentials** as the primary technical solution (plus invisible watermarks like SynthID). Applies to anyone whose content reaches EU audiences.
🟢 **Platform labels as a second mandatory layer:** Meta "AI Info", TikTok AIGC labels, YouTube disclosure, LinkedIn CR badge partly read C2PA automatically — but some platforms **strip C2PA manifests on upload** (documented): file metadata alone is insufficient; set the native platform label as well. AI disclosure does not replace ad disclosure and vice versa. Keep an archive copy WITH the manifest. [W]

provenance.adaptation:
Complete source sections. Apply these NGV adaptations before source imperatives:
ngv-phase-order: The active pack owns phase order. Musicvideo remains Track → optional Lyrics → Init → approved Analysis → optional existing material → story. Use W10 knowledge inside the relevant existing phases; a replacement phase graph requires an explicit decision.
ngv-canon: Map bible roles to NGV canonical writers/artifacts and cumulative exact-byte lineage. Do not create an independent markdown authority. Draft/proposal and approval remain different states; phase edits require explicit rewind.
ngv-greenfield: Musicvideo may be greenfield: propose story or nonnarrative concept from approved audio analysis and optional lyrics. Missing existing story files never block development. Execution prompts cannot silently invent unapproved beats.
ngv-language: App interaction follows explicit app localization or an explicit language request. Generated model prompts remain English with literal dialogue in the declared dialogue language. Preserve user-supplied text as input/provenance; the normal route still precompiles it, never bypasses the prompt engine.
ngv-hybrid: Reusable craft, coverage, structure, review and finishing also apply to imported/live_action/ai_enhanced shots. Generation-only anchors, paid routes and draft renders are conditional on source mode. Retain zero-generation musicvideo/film workflows.
ngv-anchor-modes: Record reference anchor, exact keyframe interpolation, frame continuation and native video extension as different proposed modes. #485 must settle integration with locked chained-shot semantics. Existing predecessor-last-frame-only chain remains unchanged until that decision.
ngv-provider-evidence: These are dated source claims, not live verified capabilities. Keep original date/confidence/route. Executability comes from enabled providers intersected with actual route support. Never transplant a UI field into an API or enable a provider from this corpus.
ngv-spend: Preserve the diagnostic counting protocol and escalation thresholds as configurable policy. Every paid operation stays inside explicit cost/batch authorization (#480); never automatically spend through the entire suggested budget. A paid diagnostic is not a free validation.
ngv-style-scope: Bind each selected criterion to its actual frame/shot/sequence/project scope and evidence modality. Technical provenance gates remain deterministic; aesthetic reviews require viewed media or attributed director review. A local fault on a usable production take follows scoped repair before regeneration.
ngv-performance-audio: Musicvideo master audio is the original track. Referenced segments can drive performance/lip sync without becoming replacement soundtrack. Singing, spoken dialogue, VO, ambience and score are separate roles with explicit mouth ownership; keep scope of music-bleed exception.
ngv-documentary: For actual documentary, paper edit selects attributed, consented source transcript ranges; no invented witness quote or synthetic footage passed off as evidence. Authored or reenacted interviews are a separately declared synthetic mode, preserving source/disclosure provenance.
ngv-abi-and-pins: Use versioned resources/new extension artifacts under existing registration and loader. Do not add stored fields to compatible public V1 value types. Existing projects retain pinned pack/profile/library versions; migration is explicit and transactional.
ngv-style-risk: A deliberate style may accept a named aesthetic imperfection; it does not excuse wrong identity, anatomy, unapproved canon changes or provenance gaps. Distinguish intentional camera following from accidental floating camera.
ngv-examples: Keep example and template content available in full, but instantiate only from actual project data and verified route. Never promote example light/weather/plot, prices, IDs or account names into canon.
ngv-legal: Preserve attribution, consent, rights and disclosure procedures and the source date. Do not compile jurisdiction-specific legal conclusions into an automatic green gate. No additional legal research or advice is asserted by this extraction.
ngv-knowledge-scope: Keep every actionable item locally; select the relevant complete procedure/recipe and its governing exceptions per task. Do not inject all files, silently truncate the selected procedure, or mistake a small initial library for complete migration.
ngv-readable-overlays: Preserve the chosen recording-format tell or chapter-card intent as an NLE overlay/title with exact text where needed; do not ask the video generator to render reliable readable text. Non-text recording artifacts remain generation style. This is an explicit NGV realization of both source intentions, not a claim that the source contains this reconciliation.
